sets.relationshipLabel: thing and the feature it always has
sets.explanation: A piton always has an eye and a carabiner always has a gate — each object named alongside the part that defines its function.

sets.relationshipLabel: category of peak and a named member of it
sets.explanation: Eight-thousander and fourteener are altitude categories, with K2 and Rainier standing as their real-world examples.

sets.relationshipLabel: worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A belayer is defined by their belay device just as a lead climber is defined by the rack they carry.

sets.relationshipLabel: opening stage of the larger whole it belongs to
sets.explanation: The approach opens a route and the basecamp opens an expedition — each is the first phase of something bigger, not a separate thing.

glossary.definition: A mountain whose summit rises above 8,000 meters, a rare height only a handful of peaks on Earth reach.
